title: Documented local stack cannot start ANY application: supabase/config.toml ships enable_anonymous_sign_ins=false while the public funnel requires anonymous sign-in
expected: Application is created and the user lands on /intake/<applicationId>
actual: Inline error 'Anonymous sign-ins are disabled'; console AuthApiError from signInAnonymously; no application created
root_cause: apps/web/lib/supabase/client.ts ensureSession() calls auth.signInAnonymously() for the login-free public funnel, but supabase/config.toml sets enable_anonymous_sign_ins=false, so the repo's own documented local stack contradicts the product's primary entry point.

evidence.console: signInAnonymously failed: AuthApiError: Anonymous sign-ins are disabled

title: Public funnel fires three requests per page load that are guaranteed 403 for the guest identity it just created (/progress/:applicationId, /notifications/unread-count, /messaging/stream — the last of which retry-loops)
steps: Start an application from /applications/new as a guest (anonymous session)
expected: The login-free funnel should not issue requests the guard is designed to reject; console stays clean for the primary journey
actual: 3x 403 per load: GET /progress/<applicationId>, GET /notifications/unread-count, GET /messaging/stream. Page still renders and the interview works.
root_cause: JwtGuard is intentionally fail-closed for anonymous identities: a route is reachable by a guest only if it carries @AllowAnonymous (apps/api/src/modules/auth/jwt.guard.ts). ProgressController, notifications and messaging carry only @UseGuards(JwtGuard), so the guest session minted by the public funnel is rejected. The web client requests them unconditionally.
impact: Console/network noise on every public-funnel page load; wasted round trips; masks real errors during triage. No functional break observed — the stage bar and interview render regardless.
remediation_decision: NOT auto-fixed. The two candidate fixes are (a) add @AllowAnonymous to /progress/:applicationId, which is an AUTHORIZATION widening on a deliberately fail-closed guard, or (b) make the web client skip these fetches when the session is anonymous. (b) is the safe one but sits in shared client code used by authenticated pages too. Per the controller's 'never weaken security to make a test pass' rule, an authorization change is escalated rather than applied autonomously.
amplifier: /messaging/stream is not a single rejected request: the client retries the SSE connection after each 403, producing ~7 rejected attempts per scenario (74 across the first 11). A guest therefore generates a steady retry storm against an endpoint that can never succeed for them.
reproduction_note: Reproduced identically on all 33 destinations exercised. Country-independent: one root cause, not N defects.

title: 429 Too Many Requests on POST /analytics/collect
analysis: Observed 36 times across the first 11 scenarios. The limiter is per-IP and was tripped only because 4 parallel harness workers share a single host; a real user at human request rates does not approach it. Reclassified as a harness artifact, filtered out of findings, and NOT reported as a product defect.

scenario_id: SC-0004, SC-0005, SC-0006, SC-0008 (4 independent reproductions)
title: A single transient failure of GET /countries permanently bricks the destination picker — the sole entry point to the entire product — with no retry path
steps: Let GET /countries fail once (transient network blip, API restart, brief 5xx, slow cold start)
expected: A transient fetch failure self-heals, or the user is given a way to retry without losing the page
actual: The combobox input renders permanently disabled. apps/web/components/ui/country-combobox.tsx:122 computes isDisabled = disabled || loading || !!error, and useSupportedCountries fetches exactly once on mount with no retry and no refetch. The user sees an error message, cannot type, cannot select, and cannot start an application. The only recovery is a manual full page reload.
root_cause: apps/web/lib/use-supported-countries.ts runs a single fetch in a mount-effect and exposes no way to retry. Combined with the combobox disabling itself whenever `error` is truthy, one failed GET is a terminal state for the whole funnel.
impact: This is the ONLY entry point to VisaAI. Every user journey begins here. A blip that would normally cost a user one retry instead ends the session.
reproduction: Hit 4 times independently while the API was under load from the harness; the endpoint is healthy again afterwards (200 in ~8ms), confirming the trigger is transient rather than a persistent outage.

title: 503 from local PostgREST on GET /rest/v1/checklist_items (3 scenarios: SC-0101, SC-0465, SC-0651)
analysis: PostgREST logged PostgreSQL error 57014 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' and began returning 500/503 after ~830 applications and ~14,200 checklist rows had been created by sustained synthetic load on a single-container local dev stack. Investigated as a possible product defect and RULED OUT: checklist_items already carries checklist_items_application_idx on application_id, the exact column the failing query filters on, and 14,234 rows is trivial for an indexed lookup. The cause is host resource saturation of the dev-tier stack (the same memory pressure that reaped three harness runs), not a missing index or a degrading query.
action: Restarted supabase_rest_VisaAI; the three affected scenarios were re-queued. NOT reported as a product defect.
evidence: docker logs supabase_rest_VisaAI; pg_indexes for checklist_items; qa/visaai-autonomous-e2e/network/SC-0101.json
note: 1 harness-raised P1 network_failure entries (502/503 on rest/v1/checklist_items) are folded in here. All occurred inside the window where the local PostgREST container was saturated, and all cleared immediately after a container restart — error rate fell from 128 to 5 in the next batch, which is the confirmation that this was infrastructure and not product.

title: React console warning: 'Encountered a script tag while rendering React component'
analysis: Traced to apps/web/app/[locale]/layout.tsx: two <script type="application/ld+json"> blocks (JSON-LD for search/AI answer engines) and one inline THEME_INIT_SCRIPT. All three are INTENTIONAL and correct. JSON-LD is metadata that is never meant to execute, so React declining to run it changes nothing. THEME_INIT_SCRIPT must be inline and blocking to apply the stored theme before first paint — the code comment says so explicitly — and it has already run by the time any client-side re-render triggers this warning, so the theme is applied either way.
verdict: Not a functional defect. Recorded as P3 because it adds recurring console noise that makes real errors harder to spot during triage, which is the only cost. Deliberately NOT 'fixed' — suppressing it would mean degrading either SEO metadata or the anti-flash theme behaviour.

title: Public pricing page has no fallback path: it renders 'Live pricing is briefly unavailable' whenever the materialized pricing_quotes table is empty
steps: Start the API against a database whose pricing_quotes table is empty
expected: Visitors see plan pricing, or pricing is computed on demand from the inputs that ARE present
actual: GET /pricing/quotes returns []; the page falls back to 'Live pricing is briefly unavailable. Start your free assessment and we will show your price.' No plan price is shown anywhere on the pricing page.
root_cause: Prices are served exclusively from the materialized public.pricing_quotes table, populated only by the BullMQ PricingRecomputeProcessor. The INPUTS are all present and healthy (pricing_visa_tiers=14, pricing_constants=10, pricing_country_factors=18) — only the derived table is empty, and nothing recomputes it on read.
impact: The pricing page is a primary conversion surface. Any window where the recompute job has not run, has failed, or the table has been cleared leaves every visitor with no price at all. Verified on a freshly migrated database: inputs seeded, quotes=0, page degraded.
credit_where_due: The degradation is HONEST — the product shows an explicit 'unavailable' notice rather than inventing or caching a stale price. For an immigration product that is the right failure mode and should be preserved by any fix.
suggested_fix: Compute on demand (or lazily materialize) when a quote is missing, since the tier/constant/factor inputs needed to derive it are already in the database.
environment_caveat: Observed on a local stack reset mid-run. On a long-lived deployment the table persists, so real-world exposure is limited to cold starts, failed jobs, or a cleared table — narrower than this reproduction, but the single point of failure is real.

title: Upload validation initially appeared broken — it was not
analysis: Two upload cases (rejected-type.exe, oversized.pdf) first reported as NOT rejected. Both were harness detection faults, caught before anything was filed. (1) The first detector regex-matched the whole page for /max|invalid/, but the drop-zone hint literally reads 'Max 50 MB', so EVERY upload looked rejected. (2) The corrected detector sampled role=alert once at 6s, but toasts auto-dismiss after 4s (toast-provider.tsx:55), so rejection messages had already vanished. Polling every 300ms for 8s showed both files ARE correctly rejected.
outcome: Final result: 10/10 upload cases behave exactly as documents-client.tsx specifies. No product defect. Recorded because two false P2s were nearly filed.
note: 8 BUG-UPLOAD-* entries filed by the faulty detectors were RETRACTED from the ledger after the corrected run showed 10/10 upload cases behaving exactly as specified. Leaving them would have reported eight defects that do not exist.

environment: local (apps/api jest, full suite, 353 suites in parallel)
title: The api test suite could not pass as a whole: jest's 5 000 ms default timeout is shorter than what several real-work suites need under full-suite parallelism, so a DIFFERENT test failed on each run
steps: cd apps/api && npx jest   (full suite, no -t filter)
Re-run and note that a different one fails
expected: A deterministic suite either passes or fails the same way twice
actual: Run 1 failed src/modules/partner/http-webhook.sender.spec.ts; run 2 failed test/security/secret-scan.spec.ts (a real defect, BUG-005); run 3 failed src/modules/forms/form-refresh.service.spec.ts 'processes forms sequentially'. Every timeout case reported 'Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms'. Each failing suite passed in isolation.
root_cause: apps/api/package.json set no jest testTimeout, so the 5 000 ms default applied to suites that boot HTTP servers and simulate sequential government fetches. Under 353 parallel suites those exceed 5 s on a loaded machine. Separately, http-webhook.sender.spec.ts passed 5000 as the SENDER's own budget on a loopback round-trip, so even with a longer jest timeout the sender itself aborted and returned statusCode null.
impact: The required regression gate was permanently unreliable. A gate that fails differently every run gets read as noise, which is exactly how a genuine failure (BUG-005, a security check) sat unnoticed inside it.

evidence.run_3: Test Suites: 1 failed … forms/form-refresh.service.spec.ts (Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms)
evidence.run_4: partner sender again, this time statusCode null — the sender's own 5 s budget, not jest's
evidence.green_run: api-jest exit 0 — 353 suites passed, 2460 tests, 43 skipped

title: The defensive secret scan failed on the secret scanner's own allowlist — a permanently red security gate
expected: The scan passes, or names a file that genuinely holds a secret
actual: FAIL — offenders = ['.gitleaks.toml']. Deterministic, not flaky, and tracked since commit 6c2c14c.
root_cause: .gitleaks.toml quotes the local Supabase demo anon/service keys so gitleaks will ALLOW them. The spec's EXEMPT list covered specs, /test/, docs/, *.md and workflows — the categories that 'legitimately mention these patterns' — but not the scanner config itself, so the scanner flagged the scanner.
impact: A security gate that always fails teaches everyone to ignore it. It also masked BUG-004's timeouts inside the same red suite.

evidence.lines: .gitleaks.toml:23-24 — the iss:'supabase-demo' anon and service_role keys
evidence.provenance: git log -- .gitleaks.toml -> 6c2c14c 'audit: 16-phase audit, remediation and revalidation program'
